subject.title: fix(line): bound inbound media download body reads

question: Should LINE inbound media fail closed after a fixed 120-second post-header body deadline even though the current LINE handler may degrade a transient timeout rather than retry it through durable ingress?
rationale: The code and loopback proof support a bounded-stream mechanism, but selecting a universal timeout and accepting the resulting delivery behavior requires ownership of LINE’s user-facing retry/degrade policy.

options.title: Accept the 120-second body deadline
options.body: Land the PR as a bounded fail-closed transfer policy and handle durable retry classification separately in the existing LINE ingress follow-up.

options.title: Adjust the policy before merge
options.body: Choose a different LINE-specific budget or a retry-aware timeout classification before adding a deadline that can degrade slow but otherwise valid media.

options.title: Pause for the ingress-retry fix
options.body: Defer this timeout change until the transient download failure path can return retryable errors to the durable ingress drain.

recommendation.title: Accept the 120-second body deadline
recommendation.body: Land the PR as a bounded fail-closed transfer policy and handle durable retry classification separately in the existing LINE ingress follow-up.

likelyOwner.reason: They introduced the current LINE 202/readiness download contract and are the strongest history-based routing candidate for its delivery semantics.
